goal.sl: Rečeš someone, anything, nothing, everywhere s prvim delom po pravilu some in any, uporabiš samo eno nikalnico (I saw nothing, I didn't see anything) in dodaš something nice ali anything else.
goal.de: Du sagst someone, anything, nothing, everywhere, mit dem ersten Teil nach der Regel von some und any, nimmst nur eine Verneinung (I saw nothing, I didn't see anything) und sagst something nice oder anything else.
goal.it: Dici someone, anything, nothing, everywhere, con la prima parte secondo la regola di some e any, usi una sola negazione (I saw nothing, I didn't see anything) e aggiungi something nice o anything else.
goal.en: You can say someone, anything, nothing, everywhere, the first part by the rule of some and any, use one negative only (I saw nothing, I didn't see anything), and add something nice or anything else.

say.sl: **some-** je za trdilne stavke: **someone** (nekdo; **somebody** je isto), **something** (nekaj), **somewhere** (nekje). **Someone is at the door.** (Nekdo je pri vratih.) **I've got something for you.** (Nekaj imam zate.) **Meg is somewhere on the fell.** (Meg je nekje na hribu.)
say.de: **some-** steht im bejahten Satz: **someone** (jemand; **somebody** ist dasselbe), **something** (etwas), **somewhere** (irgendwo). **Someone is at the door.** (Jemand ist an der Tür.) **I've got something for you.** (Ich habe etwas für dich.) **Meg is somewhere on the fell.** (Meg ist irgendwo am Berg.)
say.it: **some-** è per le frasi affermative: **someone** (qualcuno; **somebody** è lo stesso), **something** (qualcosa), **somewhere** (da qualche parte). **Someone is at the door.** (C'è qualcuno alla porta.) **I've got something for you.** (Ho qualcosa per te.) **Meg is somewhere on the fell.** (Meg è da qualche parte sul monte.)
say.en: **some-** is for a yes sentence: **someone** (**somebody** is the same), **something**, **somewhere**. **Someone is at the door.** **I've got something for you.** **Meg is somewhere on the fell.**

examples.en: Meg is somewhere on the fell.
examples.it: Meg è da qualche parte sul monte.

say.sl: **any-** je za zanikane stavke in večino vprašanj: **anyone** (kdo, nihče; tudi **anybody**), **anything** (kaj, nič), **anywhere** (kje, nikjer). **I can't see anyone.** (Nikogar ne vidim.) **Did you buy anything?** (Si kaj kupil{m:|f:a}?) **Is there anywhere to eat?** (Je kje kaj za jesti?) Ponudba ostane pri **some-**: **Would you like something to drink?** (Bi kaj popil{m:|f:a}?)
say.de: **any-** steht im verneinten Satz und in den meisten Fragen: **anyone** (jemand, niemand; auch **anybody**), **anything** (etwas, nichts), **anywhere** (irgendwo, nirgends). **I can't see anyone.** (Ich sehe niemanden.) **Did you buy anything?** (Hast du etwas gekauft?) **Is there anywhere to eat?** (Kann man hier irgendwo essen?) Das Angebot bleibt bei **some-**: **Would you like something to drink?** (Möchtest du etwas trinken?)
say.it: **any-** è per le frasi negative e per la maggior parte delle domande: **anyone** (qualcuno, nessuno; anche **anybody**), **anything** (qualcosa, niente), **anywhere** (da qualche parte). **I can't see anyone.** (Non vedo nessuno.) **Did you buy anything?** (Hai comprato qualcosa?) **Is there anywhere to eat?** (C'è un posto per mangiare?) L'offerta resta con **some-**: **Would you like something to drink?** (Vuoi qualcosa da bere?)
say.en: **any-** is for a no sentence and most questions: **anyone** (**anybody**), **anything**, **anywhere**. **I can't see anyone.** **Did you buy anything?** **Is there anywhere to eat?** An offer keeps **some-**: **Would you like something to drink?**

examples.en: Did you buy anything at the market?
examples.de: Hast du auf dem Markt etwas gekauft?

examples.en: Would you like something to drink?

say.sl: **no-** ima ne že v sebi, zato je glagol trdilen: **no one** (nihče; tudi **nobody**), **nothing** (nič), **nowhere** (nikjer). **I saw nothing.** je isto kot **I didn't see anything.** (Nič nisem videl{m:|f:a}.) Samo ena nikalnica, ne kot v slovenščini: nikoli *I didn't see nothing.*
say.de: **no-** hat das Nein schon in sich, das Verb bleibt bejaht: **no one** (niemand; auch **nobody**), **nothing** (nichts), **nowhere** (nirgends). **I saw nothing.** ist dasselbe wie **I didn't see anything.** (Ich habe nichts gesehen.) Nur eine Verneinung: nie *I didn't see nothing.*
say.it: **no-** ha già il no dentro, quindi il verbo resta affermativo: **no one** (nessuno; anche **nobody**), **nothing** (niente), **nowhere** (da nessuna parte). **I saw nothing.** è come **I didn't see anything.** (Non ho visto niente.) Una sola negazione, non come in italiano: mai *I didn't see nothing.*
say.en: **no-** has the no in it, so the verb stays yes: **no one** (**nobody**), **nothing**, **nowhere**. **I saw nothing.** is the same as **I didn't see anything.** One negative only: **I didn't see anything.** (never *I didn't see nothing.*)

examples.en: I didn't see anything on the fell.

examples.it: Sul monte non ho visto niente.

say.sl: **every-** je za vse: **everyone** (vsi; tudi **everybody**), **everything** (vse), **everywhere** (povsod). Glagol je v ednini: **Everyone is at the inn.** (Vsi so v gostilni.), nikoli *Everyone are.* **Everything is ready.** (Vse je pripravljeno.) **There's snow everywhere.** (Povsod je sneg.)
say.de: **every-** steht für alle: **everyone** (alle; auch **everybody**), **everything** (alles), **everywhere** (überall). Das Verb steht im Singular: **Everyone is at the inn.** (Alle sind im Gasthaus.), nie *Everyone are.* **Everything is ready.** (Alles ist bereit.) **There's snow everywhere.** (Überall liegt Schnee.)
say.it: **every-** è per tutti: **everyone** (tutti; anche **everybody**), **everything** (tutto), **everywhere** (dappertutto). Il verbo è al singolare: **Everyone is at the inn.** (Sono tutti alla locanda.), mai *Everyone are.* **Everything is ready.** (È tutto pronto.) **There's snow everywhere.** (C'è neve dappertutto.)
say.en: **every-** is for all: **everyone** (**everybody**), **everything**, **everywhere**. The verb is singular: **Everyone is at the inn.** (never *Everyone are at the inn.*) **Everything is ready.** **There's snow everywhere.**

examples.en: Everyone is at the inn tonight.
examples.de: Heute Abend sind alle im Gasthaus.

say.sl: **No one** in **nothing** lahko stojita sama ali na začetku stavka: **Who's there? — No one.** (Kdo je tam? — Nihče.) **What did you buy? — Nothing.** (Kaj si kupil{m:|f:a}? — Nič.) **Where did you go? — Nowhere.** (Kam si {m:šel|f:šla}? — Nikamor.) **No one came.** (Nihče ni prišel.), nikoli *Anyone didn't come.*
say.de: **No one** und **nothing** können allein oder am Satzanfang stehen: **Who's there? — No one.** (Wer ist da? — Niemand.) **What did you buy? — Nothing.** (Was hast du gekauft? — Nichts.) **Where did you go? — Nowhere.** (Wohin bist du gegangen? — Nirgendwohin.) **No one came.** (Niemand ist gekommen.), nie *Anyone didn't come.*
say.it: **No one** e **nothing** possono stare da soli o all'inizio della frase: **Who's there? — No one.** (Chi c'è? — Nessuno.) **What did you buy? — Nothing.** (Che cosa hai comprato? — Niente.) **Where did you go? — Nowhere.** (Dove sei andat{m:o|f:a}? — Da nessuna parte.) **No one came.** (Non è venuto nessuno.), mai *Anyone didn't come.*
say.en: **No one** and **nothing** can stand alone or open a sentence: **Who's there? — No one.** **What did you buy? — Nothing.** **Where did you go? — Nowhere.** **No one came.** (never *Anyone didn't come.*)

examples.it: Dove sei andat{m:o|f:a}? — Da nessuna parte.

say.sl: Pridevnik ali **to** + glagol pride za njimi: **something nice** (nekaj lepega), **nothing new** (nič novega), **something to eat** (nekaj za pojesti), **nowhere to sleep** (nikjer prostora za spanje). **else** pomeni drug: **anything else?** (še kaj?), **someone else** (nekdo drug).
say.de: Ein Adjektiv oder **to** + Verb kommt danach: **something nice** (etwas Schönes), **nothing new** (nichts Neues), **something to eat** (etwas zu essen), **nowhere to sleep** (kein Platz zum Schlafen). **else** heißt sonst: **anything else?** (sonst noch etwas?), **someone else** (jemand anders).
say.it: Un aggettivo o **to** + verbo viene dopo: **something nice** (qualcosa di bello), **nothing new** (niente di nuovo), **something to eat** (qualcosa da mangiare), **nowhere to sleep** (nessun posto per dormire). **else** vuol dire altro: **anything else?** (altro?), **someone else** (qualcun altro).
say.en: An adjective or **to** + a verb comes after them: **something nice** (never *something of nice*), **nothing new**, **something to eat**, **nowhere to sleep**. **else** means other: **anything else?**, **someone else**.

examples.en: Mrs Birkett made something nice for the walkers.
examples.sl: Gospa Birkett je pripravila nekaj lepega za pohodnike.
examples.de: Frau Birkett hat etwas Schönes für die Wanderer gemacht.
examples.it: La signora Birkett ha preparato qualcosa di buono per gli escursionisti.

exercises.text: Last night ___ took Mr Dixon's hammer. — Did you see ___, Mr Dixon? — No, I saw ___. I heard ___ at the door, but there was ___ there. — Did ___ at the inn hear ___? — No. ___ was asleep.

translation.sl: Sinoči je nekdo vzel kladivo gospoda Dixona. — Ste koga videli, gospod Dixon? — Ne, nič nisem videl. Pri vratih sem nekaj slišal, a tam ni bilo nikogar. — Je kdo v gostilni kaj slišal? — Ne. Vsi so spali.
translation.de: Gestern Nacht hat jemand Herrn Dixons Hammer genommen. — Haben Sie jemanden gesehen, Herr Dixon? — Nein, ich habe nichts gesehen. Ich habe etwas an der Tür gehört, aber da war niemand. — Hat jemand im Gasthaus etwas gehört? — Nein. Alle haben geschlafen.
translation.it: Ieri notte qualcuno ha preso il martello del signor Dixon. — Ha visto qualcuno, signor Dixon? — No, non ho visto niente. Ho sentito qualcosa alla porta, ma non c'era nessuno. — Qualcuno alla locanda ha sentito qualcosa? — No. Dormivano tutti.
translation.en: Last night someone took Mr Dixon's hammer. — Did you see anyone, Mr Dixon? — No, I saw nothing. I heard something at the door, but there was no one there. — Did anyone at the inn hear anything? — No. Everyone was asleep.

translation.en: There's a dance at the inn tonight, and everyone is there. Mr Tyson can't find anywhere to sit. — Is there anything to eat, Mrs Birkett? — Sorry, there's nothing left. — Can I have something to drink, then?
